cards.front: What is the size of the magnetic force on a moving charge, and what does each symbol mean?
cards.back: $F_B=|q|vB\sin\theta$ gives the **magnetic force** in newtons, where $q$ is charge, $v$ is speed, $B$ is field strength, and $\theta$ is the angle between velocity and field.
cards.hint: Think about when the force is largest.

cards.front: What are the steps of the right-hand rule for the force on a positive charge?
cards.back: Point your **fingers** along the velocity, curl them toward the field, and your **thumb** points along the force. A negative charge feels the opposite direction.
cards.hint: Start with your fingers, not your thumb.

cards.front: Why can a magnetic force never change the speed of a charged particle?
cards.back: The force is always **perpendicular** to the velocity, so it does no work. It changes only the direction of motion, not the speed.
cards.hint: Think about the angle between the force and the motion.

cards.front: What produces a magnetic field, and does a charge at rest make one?
cards.back: A **moving charge** produces a magnetic field, because current is charge in motion. A charge at rest has no magnetic field.

cards.front: What is a uniform magnetic field?
cards.back: A **uniform magnetic field** has the same strength and the same direction at every point in the region.

cards.front: A proton moves at $3.0\times10^{6}\,\mathrm{m/s}$ perpendicular to a $0.50\,\mathrm{T}$ field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force?
cards.hint: Perpendicular means the sine of the angle is 1.

cards.front: A student says a magnetic field can speed up a charged particle moving across it. What is wrong with this?
cards.back: **Wrong**: the force is perpendicular to the velocity, so it cannot speed the particle up or slow it down. It only bends the path.
cards.hint: Check what the force does to the velocity.

cards.front: An electron moves right in a field directed into the page. A student says the force points up the page. What is the error?
cards.back: The student forgot the **negative charge**. The rule gives up for a positive charge, so an electron feels a force **down** the page.
cards.hint: Check the sign of the charge first.

cards.front: What is the radius of the circular path of a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field?
cards.back: $r=\frac{mv}{|q|B}$, where $m$ is **mass**, $v$ is speed, $|q|$ is charge size, and $B$ is field strength. The radius grows with mass and speed.
cards.hint: Set the magnetic force equal to the force toward the center.

cards.front: How can a magnetic field sort particles that all travel at the same speed?
cards.back: Particles with a larger **mass-to-charge ratio** follow larger circles, so the field separates them by that ratio.
cards.hint: Look at what the radius formula depends on.

cards.front: What is the radius of a proton's path in a $0.50\,\mathrm{T}$ field at $3.0\times10^{6}\,\mathrm{m/s}$, given its mass is $1.67\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg}$?
What path does a charge follow if its velocity has a component along the magnetic field?
cards.back: The along-field component feels no force, so the path becomes a **spiral** around the field direction.
